scope.market_definition: The Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Beacon market encompasses devices that utilize BLE technology to transmit signals to nearby devices, enabling location-based services and proximity marketing. Key participants include manufacturers of BLE beacons, distributors, and various channel partners that facilitate the deployment and integration of these devices across different sectors globally.

value_chain_layers.description: This layer involves the production of BLE beacons and related hardware.
This layer includes the distribution and wholesale of BLE beacons to various markets.
Channel partners provide integration and service solutions for BLE beacons.

#### How does it work?

UWB Tags are handy little gadgets that can detect other nearby tags with inch-level precision. They
can trigger actions based on how close they are to each other. With built-in IMU and pressure
sensors, they can also track movement and elevation. They can send real-time location and other data
over LTE directly to your endpoints, making them a perfect platform for asset tracking, productivity
and safety applications.

40

#### What are they used for?

They are used to easily and precisely locate things both indoors and outdoors. Since they are
programmable and have connectivity, they are often used for automation. For example, team members
can wear them and things can happen automatically just by entering different rooms or approaching
equipment.

[Download PDF with 200+ use-cases][2]

#### How do they work technically?

Each UWB Tag has a very precise clock and an ultra wideband transmitter. When they communicate, they
measure the time these radio signals travel from one to another. By multiplying this time by the
speed of light, they estimate distances to each other with inch-level accuracy. This precision
allows them to deliver magical experiences or automations.

#### Why I should buy this dev kit?

It is simply the best way to learn and evaluate UWB technology. You don't need embedded engineering
skills since you can program UWB tags in JavaScript direcly from your laptop. You can use them to
prototype various use cases, from asset tracking to smart badges. Since they have LTE, you can also

#### What is the battery life of a UWB tag?

Each tag has a 400 mAh rechargeable battery. Battery life depends on the configuration. For simple
UWB or BLE beaconing, they can last years on a single charge. When programmed to act as wearables
detecting proximity and sending data, they can last a few weeks. For continuous scanning and
real-time asset tracking, they require permanent power via USB-C.

#### How accurate are the tags?

It depends on tag orientation, but on average, without any filtering, you should expect approx.
20cm. With sensor fusion including the IMU, accuracy could improve to sub-10cm. Their responsiveness
can be as low as 10ms, and the range is up to 30-40m, extendable to 100-200m with an LNA amplifier.

#### Do they work in any environment?

UWB signals are 3-9 GHz frequency and can easily go through concrete, wood or glass. As every radio
wave it might be blocked by metal structures so in a complex industrial environments it is important
to install more of them to ensure line of sight. They be deployed indoor or outdoor and they survive
from -40°C up to +40°C.

# Asset Tracking, powered by your frontline

Blecon enables frontline devices as BLE Tracking Agents

[Blecon Asset Tracking with Blecon Track, Asset Tags and Blecon Agent]

## Bluetooth tracking that works alongside your team. Continuous ambient data capture to track asset
## location & condition in real time.

[Tracking network running on existing devices]

##### **Runs on devices your team already carries**

Unlock the Bluetooth in frontline devices as your asset tracking network.

[Asset coverage that extends beyond fixed infrastructure]

##### **Collect data everywhere you operate**

Runs in the background, collecting data wherever your teams operates.

[Offline data capture with logger Tags]

##### **Coverage gaps don't have to mean data gaps
##### **

Tags can log timestamped sensor data offline, then upload when in range.

[Live exceptions and alerts]

##### **Know what to act on, in time to act**

Rules, alerts and APIs to allow people and systems to react and analyse.

## **Runs on devices your team already carries**

No readers, scanners or gateways to install. No cabling. No workflow change for staff. Blecon Agent
runs in the background on the devices your team already uses capturing location and sensor data
automatically. Because the network is built on devices you control rather than someone else's
consumer phones, it's deployable, scalable and dependable for operational use.

[Blecon Agent running on a Zebra handheld device used by a warehouse operative]
 

## Collect data everywhere you operate

Wherever your team operates, from warehouse floors to hospital wards, from vehicle cabs to customer
sites, every frontline device running Blecon Agent picks up tag signals as they move through their
day, capturing location and condition automatically. The Network's shape grows with your team.




[Asset tracking coverage following pallets and shipments across multiple sites and transit lanes]
 

## Coverage gaps don't have to mean data gaps

Some assets go where coverage doesn't follow: deep inside a refrigerated container or on a long-haul
route. For those journeys, Blecon's Logging Tags capture location and temperature data on the Tag
itself. When the asset comes back within range, the full record uploads. You see where it went and
what happened to it along the way.

[Refrigerated lorry on a long-haul route with Blecon logger Tags capturing temperature and location
data inside the trailer]
 

## Know what to act on, in time to act.

Blecon Track turns Tag data into the specific alerts your operation needs: a temperature breach, an
asset leaving an authorised zone, a tool not returned to base. Each alert routes to the right people
or systems the moment a condition is met. Because alerts are configured against your operational
thresholds, your team hears about it in time to act, not after the fact. 




[Operations manager reviewing live alerts and exceptions in the Blecon Track interface]

## Who we are

Bluetooth® is more than just a technology. The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) is a community
of some of the most inventive minds and organizations with the shared vision of creating a better
world through connection. Together, we advance, protect, and promote Bluetooth® technology, the
global standard for connection.

## Advance

We are an international standards development organization. We continually enhance Bluetooth®
technology by creating new specifications that push the boundaries of what’s possible and help make
the world a better place.

## Protect

We are a product certification body. We operate a world-class product qualification program that
promotes global interoperability and provides access to Bluetooth technology patent and trademark
licenses.

## Promote

We are a global trade association. We collaborate to increase the awareness, understanding, and
adoption of Bluetooth technology.

Casambi powers flexible, intelligent lighting throughout Pavion’s headquarters—seamlessly
controlling every office environment and fixture from a single, intuitive platform: LightingOS.

retrofits to new builds, Casambi thrives in any environment.

No company can realize the IoT on its own… Within the Eclipse Community, through the contribution of
many IoT developers, tools and standards are created on an open platform that many companies can
benefit from for their IoT applications.

[Picture of Stefan Ferber]

Stefan Ferber / Co-CEO and CTO, Bosch .IO GmbH

Eclipse IoT is the industry’s leading community for Open Source IoT projects. For Red Hat, Eclipse
IoT is the place where we collaborate with like-minded colleagues from other firms to create
projects that form the basis of our IoT products.

[Picture of David Ingham]

David Ingham / Director of Software Engineering, Integration Middleware, Red Hat

Within Eclipse IoT, Eurotech is working with Cloudera, Red Hat, and others to develop key IoT
runtimes and other enabling technologies that will enable integrated, end-to-end open IoT
architectures.

[Picture of Giuseppe Surace]

Giuseppe Surace / Chief Product and Marketing Officer, Eurotech

Finally, DB foresees more open source integrations in the future and looks forward to collaborating
within the Eclipse IoT Working Group. Being part of a collaboration like Eclipse IoT is a good
opportunity to improve DB’s use of open source technology, and in the long term creates better
solutions for DB passengers.

[Picture of Alexander Schmitt]

Alexander Schmitt / Chief Architect, DB-Systel

The Eclipse Foundation [puts] forth great effort to provide open source contributions in the IoT
space, which translates to vitality and enthusiasm. This is very important to us.

[Picture of Nicola La Gloria]

Nicola La Gloria / Co-founder and CEO, Kynetics

## Eclipse Foundation

The Eclipse Foundation provides individuals and organizations with a business-friendly environment
for open source software collaboration and innovation. The Foundation is home to the Eclipse IDE,
Jakarta EE, and over 375 projects, including runtimes, tools, and frameworks for IoT, edge
computing, automotive, and more. We are a not-for-profit organization supported by over 300 members.
Learn more at [eclipse.org.][19]

# Wide range of wireless sensors and an IoT platform

[Become a partner ›][131]

## Wireless sensors that suit your needs

### Bluetooth LE sensors

Over 20 types of Bluetooth Low Energy wireless sensors that communicate with smartphones, tablets or
BLE gateway. Sensors are fully compatible with Efento Cloud platform and mobile applications and can
be integrated with third party IoT platforms or mobile applications.

[Learn more][132]

### NB-IoT sensors

Efento NB-IoT sensors were developed from ground up to meet customers’ needs. Sensors measure over
20 physical and chemical values and seamlessly send the data over NB-IoT networks to Efento Cloud or
any other cloud platform. On top of that, they are equipped with all software and hardware features
a modern IoT device needs.

[Learn more][133]

# Industry4.0 - FactoryMetrics

**A Next Generation Manufacturing Intelligence Platform for Digital Factory :** Unlock smarter
manufacturing with FactoryMetrics Intelligent MES — harnessing real-time data from machines, people,
and ERP to drive efficiency and growth.

[Request Demo ][12]

## FactoryMetrics – A Smart Machine Monitoring Solution

Hiotron, FactoryMetrics (a proprietary end-to-end Industry 4.0 platform) that combines plug-and-play
IoT hardware, AI-driven analytics, and a no-code workflow layer delivers total visibility from
machine to customer, transforming manufacturing operations with intelligent, real-time insights that
drive measurable improvements in production efficiency and quality.

Case Study

## Successful Case Study : Where Technology Meets Real-World Impact

#### Rico Auto Industries Ltd – BMW Export lines Traceability System

## Project Overview

Rico Auto, a global Tier-1 partner for **BMW**, faced a critical mandate for its Gen-6 high-volume
export lines. In the high-precision automotive world, passing an OEM audit is not just about having
data; it’s about proving a “Digital Thread”—a seamless link between every machining parameter and
the final dispatched part.

## Business Challenge

Before Hiotron’s intervention, traceability relied on a “Fragmented Reality”:
1. **Data Silos:** Important information was spread across paper records, machine PLC data, and
   manual quality logs. Because the data was stored in different places, it was difficult to get one
   clear view of operations.
2. **Time-Consuming Audit Preparation: **Preparing for BMW audits took several days because teams
   had to manually collect and match records from different sources. This made the audit process
   slow, stressful, and resource-heavy.
3. **Risk of Wrong Parts Moving Forward: **Without real-time quality checks and interlocks, there
   was always a chance that a non-compliant part could move to the next stage because of human
   error. This created a serious quality and compliance risk.
4. **Limited Real-Time Traceability: **Operators, supervisors & managers did not have instant
   visibility into the journey of each component. As a result, tracking part status and identifying
   issues quickly was difficult.
5. **Weak Process Discipline at Scale: **Quality teams needed faster access to OK and NG status
   linked to each uniquely serialized part. Management also needed a reliable digital audit trail
   that could be reviewed easily, without depending on manual records. The plant required stronger
   process discipline to ensure that non-compliant parts were stopped before moving ahead.

## Hiotron Solution

Hiotron implemented an end-to-end QR and DPM scanner based part traceability solution tailored for
the **BMW** Gen-6 export lines. Each component was assigned a unique identity, and station-level
events were captured against that identity throughout the production journey.
1. **End-to-end part traceability:** Hiotron built a complete digital traceability system that
   tracked every part across the full production journey.
2. **Unique QR-based identity for every part:** Each component was linked to a unique QR code,
   making it easy to trace its status, history, and movement at any stage.
3. **Critical process and quality data capture:** The system captured important process parameters
   and quality data at every key stage and linked them to each part’s QR journey.
4. **Stage-wise interlocking for quality control:** Hiotron implemented interlocking at every stage
   so that if a part was marked **NG** or the correct process sequence was not followed, it could
   not move forward.
5. **Real-time visibility and OEE monitoring:** Operators, supervisors, and management gained live
   visibility into machine performance, production flow, and OEE for faster decision-making.
6. **One-click report export:** Part-wise, shift-wise, daily, and monthly reports could be generated
   and exported instantly, giving Rico as well as BMW audit teams a complete picture of operations
   and quality performance in just single click
7. **Stronger process discipline and audit readiness:** The solution created a reliable digital
   trail for every part, reduced manual dependency, and made audit preparation faster, easier, and
   more accurate.

## Why IN120?

Four breakthrough capabilities that make IN120 the natural choice for engineers building the next
generation of wireless sensor products.

### Sub-microwatt power draw

Operates from coin cells, thin-film batteries, or energy-harvesting sources. Intelligent duty
cycling keeps average current in the nanoamp range — power-source flexible by design.

### Integrated ±1°C accuracy

Factory-calibrated temperature sensing baked directly into the SoC — no external sensor, no
calibration, ready for cold chain and healthcare out of the box.

### Broadcast data logging

Captures and transmits sensor history autonomously over BLE advertising — even without a nearby
gateway. Your data survives dead zones.

### Near-Zero eBOM

Sensor, ADC, MCU, BLE radio, and data logger in one 1.6 × 1.6 mm chip. Single 32 MHz crystal design
— fewer parts, faster time to market.

### 2025 Annual Report

### 2025 Annual Report

**In 2025, we worked in 150 countries and territories, supporting community-centered connectivity
initiatives, helping safeguard the multistakeholder model of Internet governance, scaling our
philanthropic impact through new funding partnerships, and so much more.**

The report outlines how our global community rose to the challenge of our ambitious five-year
strategy to expand affordable, reliable access and ensure that people everywhere are safe and secure
online.

[**Read Our Report**][34]
[[Three women sit on the grass outside]][35]

### [Community-Centered Connectivity Initiatives Earn Viddy Awards Recognition][36]

**Our global community works tirelessly to expand connectivity, educate users, and build the
Internet we want—an Internet for everyone. **

We are proud to share that four videos highlighting community initiatives have won Viddy Awards this
year.
[[People stand outdoors celebrating the completion of the Internet hub in the Siripi zone, waving at
the camera.]][37]

### [From Email to Case Study: What We Learned About Connecting Refugee Communities in Just One
### Year ][38]

**In Uganda’s Rhino Camp Refugee Settlement, we helped train refugees and community members to use
the Internet and build their own networks. **

Now, two fully operational, community-owned digital hubs serve over 4,500 people.
[[A graphic showing an email notification]][39]

**Online scams are at an all-time high, and digital tools have enabled them to become more
sophisticated, more convincing, and more widespread. **

Luckily, with the right information, you can learn how to identify online scams and keep yourself
safe. Let’s take a look at some common warning signs.

Our IoT solutions for manufacturing industries optimize operations with smart sensors and real-time
data. Predictive maintenance prevents disruptions, while enhanced supply chain visibility
streamlines logistics. Embrace the future of manufacturing with our tailored, cutting-edge IoT

##### Aged care

Empower the aged care industry with our IoT solutions, featuring smart sensors and real-time data
for enhanced care services. Proactive monitoring ensures timely responses to residents needs, while
advanced safety measures prevent potential hazards. Our tailored, cutting-edge IoT technologies
create a secure and efficient environment, offering peace of mind to both caregivers and residents.
Embrace the future of aged care with our innovative solutions.

Embrace the future of agriculture with our transformative IoT solutions. Utilizing smart sensors and
real-time data analytics, we empower farmers to proactively monitor crop health and environmental
conditions, optimizing yield and resource utilization. Embrace precision agriculture practices for
sustainable farming and reduced environmental impact. Experience enhanced productivity and
efficiency with our cutting-edge technologies tailored for the agriculture industry

[See More][36]

Revolutionize the aviation industry with our comprehensive IoT solutions, integrating smart sensors,
real-time data, and a chemical inventory management system. Proactive monitoring ensures timely
maintenance responses, while predictive analytics optimizes fleet performance and safety. Manage
chemical inventory efficiently, ensuring compliance and minimizing risks. Embrace the future of
aviation with our cutting-edge, tailored IoT technologies for enhanced safety and operational
excellence

## [Anyone for Stereo Tennis?][7]
* Published[July 7, 2026July 7, 2026][8]
* [Make a comment on Anyone for Stereo Tennis?][9]

With Wimbledon upon us again, I was reminded that one of the use cases we considered when we were
designing Bluetooth LE Audio was based on a tennis audience at Centre Court.  Despite all of the
money and technology that goes into international tournaments like Wimbledon, the sound
reinforcement design provided for spectators still hasn’t evolved to the level of the original TV
tennis games of the 1960s.

Looking at the spectators sitting in the main courts, it looks as if they’re aging, possibly because
you need a hefty Civil Service defined-benefits pension to afford the tickets.  Which mean that a
fair number will have hearing loss.  According to Wimbledon’s Access Guides, there are Hearing Loops
located at key points around the grounds, but it doesn’t mention if they’re in the courts.  Even if
they are. reinforcing sound for a tennis audience poses some interesting questions.

## [Plug-in Solar and the PV Detector Van][11]
* Published[June 29, 2026][12]
* [Make a comment on Plug-in Solar and the PV Detector Van][13]

Let’s start with the good news. It looks as if the UK is about to make it legal to buy and install
plug-in solar panels.  That’s basically a solar panel packaged with electronics, that lets you plug
it directly into an ordinary 13A socket in your home to generate some of your own electricity.  The
bad news is that DESNZ ( the Department for Energy and Net Zero) want to regulate plug-in solar
units in much the same way as TVs used to be regulated.  These are DIY products which you can

billions on generating new content to attract subscribers, audio streamers are largely relying on
their back catalogues.  Whilst manufacturers and streamers have tried differentiation through
enhanced quality, specifically by providing hi-res or lossless codecs, they’ve found the take-up
disappointing, mainly because few consumers can notice the difference.

new, high quality codecs, which can sample audio at rates which only bats are likely to hear.  The

micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) speakers, capable of rendering audio at frequencies way
beyond the limits of human hearing.  This technology has led to a new generation of microphones with
frequency responses which are flat up to 100kHz – a major step forward from common studio

Многофункциональный сервис оптимизации бизнес-процессов: отказ от лишних пластиковых карт,
автоматизация сложных рутинных процессов, оптимизация рабочего времени, легкое управление, упрощение
охранных решений, сбор статистики и не только

наведите на карточку

### Пластиковая карта

Добавляйте транспортную, банковскую или любую другую пластиковую карту для прохода без
дополнительного оборудования

### Динамический QR-код

Генерируйте коды на экране телефона и просто подносите их к считывателю для открытия доступа на
предприятие/в помещение

### NFC стикеры

Используйте мобильный телефон для считывания биометрических NFC меток, наклеенных на любую
поверхность точки прохода

### Виртуальная кнопка

Нажмите на кнопку в приложении или WEB-странице, чтобы дистанционно открыть проход к любой точке
предприятия

### BLE-технология

Осуществляйте проход по территории не вынимая телефон из кармана, благодаря бесконтактной технологии
BLE

наведите на карточку

Получайте информацию о входах и выходах клиентов, персонала и эффективно организовывайте и
контролируйте каждое их перемещение внутри объекта

### Управление точками доступа

Настраивайте и управляйте любыми точками доступа на предприятии, обеспечивая бесперебойную
безопасность вашей системы охраны

### Контроль посетителей

В реальном времени контролируйте количество клиентов, а также режим доступа на объект для еще
большей безопасности

### Анализ активности

Получайте информацию о работе и эксплуатации механизма и поведении посетителей на объекте, для

## Frequently asked questions

How do I connect PPTControl to my computer?

PPTControl currently connects through Bluetooth Low Energy, also called BLE.

Bluetooth must be enabled on both devices, and PPTControl Desktop must stay open on the computer
while you use the remote.

My phone cannot find or connect to my computer. What should I do?

Make sure [PPTControl Desktop][16] is installed and open on the computer, and that Bluetooth is
enabled on both devices.

Make sure the phone and computer are not paired through normal Bluetooth settings. If they are,
remove that pairing on both devices, restart both devices, and connect again only through
PPTControl.

On Mac, also make sure the required permissions are granted. On Windows, check whether the Bluetooth
adapter supports Bluetooth Low Energy peripheral/server mode.

Can I view speaker notes in PPTControl?

Yes, with Pro, speaker notes are available for supported PowerPoint and Keynote presentations.

Open the presentation on the computer, connect PPTControl, and tap the notes icon in the mobile app.
Make sure the presentation actually contains notes and that both PPTControl apps are updated.

Which presentation apps does PPTControl support?

PPTControl is focused on **Microsoft PowerPoint**, **Apple Keynote**, and **Google Slides**.

Basic slide controls work best with the supported desktop workflows. Advanced features depend on the
presentation app and platform.

## How it Works

Wiliot connects physical items to the cloud using battery-free IoT Pixels, simple network
infrastructure, and AI-driven services. This transforms raw data into actionable insights for
smarter, more efficient operations.

###### IoT Pixels

Low-cost, battery-free Bluetooth sensors attach to items and harvest energy from ambient radio
signals to transmit data — such as location, temperature, humidity, and light.

[
Explore Wiliot IoT Pixels
][83]

###### Network Infrastructure

Off-the-shelf bridges and gateways (hubs), which are quick to deploy, wake up nearby IoT Pixels
using radio signals, receive their data, and forward it securely to the Wiliot Physical AI platform.

[
Uncover the Network Infrastructure
][84]

###### Wiliot Physical AI Platform

The Wiliot Physical AI platform is where raw sensing data is transformed into smart decisions and
where our agents and specialized AI models live. Providing alerts, analytics, and dashboards.

## How it Works

Wiliot connects physical items to the cloud using battery-free IoT Pixels, simple network
infrastructure, and AI-driven services. This transforms raw data into actionable insights for
smarter, more efficient operations.

###### IoT Pixels

Low-cost, battery-free Bluetooth sensors attach to items and harvest energy from ambient radio
signals to transmit data — such as location, temperature, humidity, and light.

[
Explore Wiliot IoT Pixels
][83]

###### Network Infrastructure

Off-the-shelf bridges and gateways (hubs), which are quick to deploy, wake up nearby IoT Pixels
using radio signals, receive their data, and forward it securely to the Wiliot Physical AI platform.

[
Uncover the Network Infrastructure
][84]

###### Wiliot Physical AI Platform

The Wiliot Physical AI platform is where raw sensing data is transformed into smart decisions and
where our agents and specialized AI models live. Providing alerts, analytics, and dashboards.

#### How does it work?

UWB Tags are handy little gadgets that can detect other nearby tags with inch-level precision. They
can trigger actions based on how close they are to each other. With built-in IMU and pressure
sensors, they can also track movement and elevation. They can send real-time location and other data
over LTE directly to your endpoints, making them a perfect platform for asset tracking, productivity
and safety applications.

40

#### What are they used for?

They are used to easily and precisely locate things both indoors and outdoors. Since they are
programmable and have connectivity, they are often used for automation. For example, team members
can wear them and things can happen automatically just by entering different rooms or approaching
equipment.

[Download PDF with 200+ use-cases][2]

#### How do they work technically?

Each UWB Tag has a very precise clock and an ultra wideband transmitter. When they communicate, they
measure the time these radio signals travel from one to another. By multiplying this time by the
speed of light, they estimate distances to each other with inch-level accuracy. This precision
allows them to deliver magical experiences or automations.

UWB is a popular emerging technology for positioning. Every Apple iPhone since 2019 has a UWB chip
that is used for precision finding, and there are 300+ million of them. Cars like Tesla and BMW use
them for keyless car entry and hands-free experiences. If you are already familiar with Bluetooth
Low Energy and its applications for IoT, beacons and proximity use-cases, you should think about UWB
as the next-gen positioning technology. It is far more accurate, equally low power, relatively
inexpensive and also easy to deploy quickly at massive scale.

detecting proximity and sending data, they can last a few weeks. For continuous scanning and
real-time asset tracking, they require permanent power via USB-C.

#### How accurate are the tags?

It depends on tag orientation, but on average, without any filtering, you should expect approx.
20cm. With sensor fusion including the IMU, accuracy could improve to sub-10cm. Their responsiveness
can be as low as 10ms, and the range is up to 30-40m, extendable to 100-200m with an LNA amplifier.

#### Do they work in any environment?

UWB signals are 3-9 GHz frequency and can easily go through concrete, wood or glass. As every radio
wave it might be blocked by metal structures so in a complex industrial environments it is important
to install more of them to ensure line of sight. They be deployed indoor or outdoor and they survive
from -40°C up to +40°C.

## **Runs on devices your team already carries**

No readers, scanners or gateways to install. No cabling. No workflow change for staff. Blecon Agent
runs in the background on the devices your team already uses capturing location and sensor data
automatically. Because the network is built on devices you control rather than someone else's
consumer phones, it's deployable, scalable and dependable for operational use.

[Blecon Agent running on a Zebra handheld device used by a warehouse operative]
 

## Collect data everywhere you operate

Wherever your team operates, from warehouse floors to hospital wards, from vehicle cabs to customer
sites, every frontline device running Blecon Agent picks up tag signals as they move through their
day, capturing location and condition automatically. The Network's shape grows with your team.




[Asset tracking coverage following pallets and shipments across multiple sites and transit lanes]
 

## Coverage gaps don't have to mean data gaps

Some assets go where coverage doesn't follow: deep inside a refrigerated container or on a long-haul
route. For those journeys, Blecon's Logging Tags capture location and temperature data on the Tag
itself. When the asset comes back within range, the full record uploads. You see where it went and
what happened to it along the way.

[Refrigerated lorry on a long-haul route with Blecon logger Tags capturing temperature and location
data inside the trailer]
 

## Know what to act on, in time to act.

Blecon Track turns Tag data into the specific alerts your operation needs: a temperature breach, an
asset leaving an authorised zone, a tool not returned to base. Each alert routes to the right people
or systems the moment a condition is met. Because alerts are configured against your operational
thresholds, your team hears about it in time to act, not after the fact. 




[Operations manager reviewing live alerts and exceptions in the Blecon Track interface]

## Who we are

Bluetooth® is more than just a technology. The Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) is a community
of some of the most inventive minds and organizations with the shared vision of creating a better
world through connection. Together, we advance, protect, and promote Bluetooth® technology, the
global standard for connection.

## Advance

We are an international standards development organization. We continually enhance Bluetooth®
technology by creating new specifications that push the boundaries of what’s possible and help make
the world a better place.

## Protect

We are a product certification body. We operate a world-class product qualification program that
promotes global interoperability and provides access to Bluetooth technology patent and trademark
licenses.

## Promote

We are a global trade association. We collaborate to increase the awareness, understanding, and
adoption of Bluetooth technology.

[Learn more][103]

No company can realize the IoT on its own… Within the Eclipse Community, through the contribution of
many IoT developers, tools and standards are created on an open platform that many companies can
benefit from for their IoT applications.

[Picture of Stefan Ferber]

Stefan Ferber / Co-CEO and CTO, Bosch .IO GmbH

Eclipse IoT is the industry’s leading community for Open Source IoT projects. For Red Hat, Eclipse
IoT is the place where we collaborate with like-minded colleagues from other firms to create
projects that form the basis of our IoT products.

[Picture of David Ingham]

David Ingham / Director of Software Engineering, Integration Middleware, Red Hat

Within Eclipse IoT, Eurotech is working with Cloudera, Red Hat, and others to develop key IoT
runtimes and other enabling technologies that will enable integrated, end-to-end open IoT
architectures.

[Picture of Giuseppe Surace]

Finally, DB foresees more open source integrations in the future and looks forward to collaborating
within the Eclipse IoT Working Group. Being part of a collaboration like Eclipse IoT is a good
opportunity to improve DB’s use of open source technology, and in the long term creates better
solutions for DB passengers.

[Picture of Alexander Schmitt]

Alexander Schmitt / Chief Architect, DB-Systel

The Eclipse Foundation [puts] forth great effort to provide open source contributions in the IoT
space, which translates to vitality and enthusiasm. This is very important to us.

## Eclipse Foundation

The Eclipse Foundation provides individuals and organizations with a business-friendly environment
for open source software collaboration and innovation. The Foundation is home to the Eclipse IDE,
Jakarta EE, and over 375 projects, including runtimes, tools, and frameworks for IoT, edge
computing, automotive, and more. We are a not-for-profit organization supported by over 300 members.

architectures.

opportunity to improve DB’s use of open source technology, and in the long term creates better
solutions for DB passengers.

The Eclipse Foundation [puts] forth great effort to provide open source contributions in the IoT

# Wide range of wireless sensors and an IoT platform

## Wireless sensors that suit your needs

### Bluetooth LE sensors

Over 20 types of Bluetooth Low Energy wireless sensors that communicate with smartphones, tablets or
BLE gateway. Sensors are fully compatible with Efento Cloud platform and mobile applications and can
be integrated with third party IoT platforms or mobile applications.

[Learn more][132]

### NB-IoT sensors

Efento NB-IoT sensors were developed from ground up to meet customers’ needs. Sensors measure over
20 physical and chemical values and seamlessly send the data over NB-IoT networks to Efento Cloud or
any other cloud platform. On top of that, they are equipped with all software and hardware features
a modern IoT device needs.

[Learn more][133]

## FactoryMetrics – A Smart Machine Monitoring Solution

Hiotron, FactoryMetrics (a proprietary end-to-end Industry 4.0 platform) that combines plug-and-play
IoT hardware, AI-driven analytics, and a no-code workflow layer delivers total visibility from
machine to customer, transforming manufacturing operations with intelligent, real-time insights that
drive measurable improvements in production efficiency and quality.

## Successful Case Study : Where Technology Meets Real-World Impact

#### Rico Auto Industries Ltd – BMW Export lines Traceability System

## Project Overview

Rico Auto, a global Tier-1 partner for **BMW**, faced a critical mandate for its Gen-6 high-volume
export lines. In the high-precision automotive world, passing an OEM audit is not just about having
data; it’s about proving a “Digital Thread”—a seamless link between every machining parameter and
the final dispatched part.

## Business Challenge

Before Hiotron’s intervention, traceability relied on a “Fragmented Reality”:
1. **Data Silos:** Important information was spread across paper records, machine PLC data, and
   manual quality logs. Because the data was stored in different places, it was difficult to get one
   clear view of operations.
2. **Time-Consuming Audit Preparation: **Preparing for BMW audits took several days because teams
   had to manually collect and match records from different sources. This made the audit process
   slow, stressful, and resource-heavy.
3. **Risk of Wrong Parts Moving Forward: **Without real-time quality checks and interlocks, there
   was always a chance that a non-compliant part could move to the next stage because of human
   error. This created a serious quality and compliance risk.
4. **Limited Real-Time Traceability: **Operators, supervisors & managers did not have instant
   visibility into the journey of each component. As a result, tracking part status and identifying
   issues quickly was difficult.
5. **Weak Process Discipline at Scale: **Quality teams needed faster access to OK and NG status
   linked to each uniquely serialized part. Management also needed a reliable digital audit trail
   that could be reviewed easily, without depending on manual records. The plant required stronger
   process discipline to ensure that non-compliant parts were stopped before moving ahead.

## Hiotron Solution

Hiotron implemented an end-to-end QR and DPM scanner based part traceability solution tailored for
the **BMW** Gen-6 export lines. Each component was assigned a unique identity, and station-level
events were captured against that identity throughout the production journey.
1. **End-to-end part traceability:** Hiotron built a complete digital traceability system that
   tracked every part across the full production journey.
2. **Unique QR-based identity for every part:** Each component was linked to a unique QR code,
   making it easy to trace its status, history, and movement at any stage.
3. **Critical process and quality data capture:** The system captured important process parameters
   and quality data at every key stage and linked them to each part’s QR journey.
4. **Stage-wise interlocking for quality control:** Hiotron implemented interlocking at every stage
   so that if a part was marked **NG** or the correct process sequence was not followed, it could
   not move forward.
5. **Real-time visibility and OEE monitoring:** Operators, supervisors, and management gained live
   visibility into machine performance, production flow, and OEE for faster decision-making.
6. **One-click report export:** Part-wise, shift-wise, daily, and monthly reports could be generated
   and exported instantly, giving Rico as well as BMW audit teams a complete picture of operations
   and quality performance in just single click
7. **Stronger process discipline and audit readiness:** The solution created a reliable digital
   trail for every part, reduced manual dependency, and made audit preparation faster, easier, and
   more accurate.

Capability

## Why IN120?

Four breakthrough capabilities that make IN120 the natural choice for engineers building the next
generation of wireless sensor products.

### Sub-microwatt power draw

Operates from coin cells, thin-film batteries, or energy-harvesting sources. Intelligent duty
cycling keeps average current in the nanoamp range — power-source flexible by design.

### Integrated ±1°C accuracy

Factory-calibrated temperature sensing baked directly into the SoC — no external sensor, no
calibration, ready for cold chain and healthcare out of the box.

### Broadcast data logging

Captures and transmits sensor history autonomously over BLE advertising — even without a nearby
gateway. Your data survives dead zones.

### Near-Zero eBOM

Sensor, ADC, MCU, BLE radio, and data logger in one 1.6 × 1.6 mm chip. Single 32 MHz crystal design
— fewer parts, faster time to market.

Capability

## Why IN120?

Four breakthrough capabilities that make IN120 the natural choice for engineers building the next
generation of wireless sensor products.

### Sub-microwatt power draw

Operates from coin cells, thin-film batteries, or energy-harvesting sources. Intelligent duty
cycling keeps average current in the nanoamp range — power-source flexible by design.

### Integrated ±1°C accuracy

Factory-calibrated temperature sensing baked directly into the SoC — no external sensor, no
calibration, ready for cold chain and healthcare out of the box.

### Broadcast data logging

Captures and transmits sensor history autonomously over BLE advertising — even without a nearby
gateway. Your data survives dead zones.

### Near-Zero eBOM

Sensor, ADC, MCU, BLE radio, and data logger in one 1.6 × 1.6 mm chip. Single 32 MHz crystal design
— fewer parts, faster time to market.

## We believe the Internet changes lives.

## But only when people can access, trust, and use it safely.

## **We’re working to connect more than 2 billion people worldwide who are still offline, and make
## the Internet safer and more trustworthy. **

[**Learn About Our Work**][33]
[Participants at a community networks training from the Haiti Chapter stand outside]
[A group of girls sitting on a sidewalk with a woman in the middle holding laptop]

### 2025 Annual Report

### 2025 Annual Report

**In 2025, we worked in 150 countries and territories, supporting community-centered connectivity
initiatives, helping safeguard the multistakeholder model of Internet governance, scaling our
philanthropic impact through new funding partnerships, and so much more.**

The report outlines how our global community rose to the challenge of our ambitious five-year
strategy to expand affordable, reliable access and ensure that people everywhere are safe and secure
online.

[**Read Our Report**][34]
[[Three women sit on the grass outside]][35]

### [Community-Centered Connectivity Initiatives Earn Viddy Awards Recognition][36]

**Our global community works tirelessly to expand connectivity, educate users, and build the
Internet we want—an Internet for everyone. **

We are proud to share that four videos highlighting community initiatives have won Viddy Awards this
year.
[[People stand outdoors celebrating the completion of the Internet hub in the Siripi zone, waving at
the camera.]][37]

### [From Email to Case Study: What We Learned About Connecting Refugee Communities in Just One
### Year ][38]

**In Uganda’s Rhino Camp Refugee Settlement, we helped train refugees and community members to use
the Internet and build their own networks. **

Now, two fully operational, community-owned digital hubs serve over 4,500 people.
[[A graphic showing an email notification]][39]

### [Anatomy of a Scam][40]

**Online scams are at an all-time high, and digital tools have enabled them to become more
sophisticated, more convincing, and more widespread. **

Luckily, with the right information, you can learn how to identify online scams and keep yourself
safe. Let’s take a look at some common warning signs.
[**Read Our Blog**][41]

## We work with these industries

##### Manufacturing

Our IoT solutions for manufacturing industries optimize operations with smart sensors and real-time
data. Predictive maintenance prevents disruptions, while enhanced supply chain visibility
streamlines logistics. Embrace the future of manufacturing with our tailored, cutting-edge IoT
solutions.

[See More][34]
[img]

##### Aged care

Empower the aged care industry with our IoT solutions, featuring smart sensors and real-time data
for enhanced care services. Proactive monitoring ensures timely responses to residents needs, while
advanced safety measures prevent potential hazards. Our tailored, cutting-edge IoT technologies
create a secure and efficient environment, offering peace of mind to both caregivers and residents.
Embrace the future of aged care with our innovative solutions.

[See More][35]
[img]

##### Healthcare

Embrace the future of agriculture with our transformative IoT solutions. Utilizing smart sensors and
real-time data analytics, we empower farmers to proactively monitor crop health and environmental
conditions, optimizing yield and resource utilization. Embrace precision agriculture practices for
sustainable farming and reduced environmental impact. Experience enhanced productivity and
efficiency with our cutting-edge technologies tailored for the agriculture industry

[See More][36]
[img]

##### Aviation

Revolutionize the aviation industry with our comprehensive IoT solutions, integrating smart sensors,
real-time data, and a chemical inventory management system. Proactive monitoring ensures timely
maintenance responses, while predictive analytics optimizes fleet performance and safety. Manage
chemical inventory efficiently, ensuring compliance and minimizing risks. Embrace the future of
aviation with our cutting-edge, tailored IoT technologies for enhanced safety and operational
excellence

[See More][37]
[img]

## [Anyone for Stereo Tennis?][7]
* Published[July 7, 2026July 7, 2026][8]
* [Make a comment on Anyone for Stereo Tennis?][9]

With Wimbledon upon us again, I was reminded that one of the use cases we considered when we were
designing Bluetooth LE Audio was based on a tennis audience at Centre Court.  Despite all of the
money and technology that goes into international tournaments like Wimbledon, the sound
reinforcement design provided for spectators still hasn’t evolved to the level of the original TV
tennis games of the 1960s.

Looking at the spectators sitting in the main courts, it looks as if they’re aging, possibly because
you need a hefty Civil Service defined-benefits pension to afford the tickets.  Which mean that a
fair number will have hearing loss.  According to Wimbledon’s Access Guides, there are Hearing Loops
located at key points around the grounds, but it doesn’t mention if they’re in the courts.  Even if
they are. reinforcing sound for a tennis audience poses some interesting questions.

[Read More][10]

## [Plug-in Solar and the PV Detector Van][11]
* Published[June 29, 2026][12]
* [Make a comment on Plug-in Solar and the PV Detector Van][13]

Let’s start with the good news. It looks as if the UK is about to make it legal to buy and install
plug-in solar panels.  That’s basically a solar panel packaged with electronics, that lets you plug
it directly into an ordinary 13A socket in your home to generate some of your own electricity.  The
bad news is that DESNZ ( the Department for Energy and Net Zero) want to regulate plug-in solar
units in much the same way as TVs used to be regulated.  These are DIY products which you can
install yourself, but when you buy one, DESNZ wants to be notified, presumably so they can check
that you’ve plugged it in properly and not broken anything.  Their proposal reads like the old TV
Licensing regime, which then sent detector vans around to make sure you had a licence.  Except in
this case, they’d be PV vans to check your Photo Voltaics.

There’s a consultation on whether that’s a good idea at
https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/plug-in-solar, but in typical DESNZ fashion, it opened
last week and closes next week.   So if you’ve got an opinion, you have until 30^{th} June to
respond.

[Read More][14]

Resistible Rise of Arturo Ui” at the Swan Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon, which I can thoroughly
recommend.   What I didn’t expect when I went to see it last week, is that I’d also learn quite a
few useful things about user experience design for hearing aids and assisted listening.

The Resistible Rise of Arturo Ui is  a parable of Hitler’s rise to power, conceived as a parallel
story based on Chicago gangsters fighting for control of the vegetable trade.  It’s an important
piece, not least because of the warning of its final line “The beast that bore him is in heat
again”.  But enough of UI for the moment.  Here’s what I learnt about User Interfaces for hearing
aids.

* Published[April 1, 2026][28]
* [Make a comment on Full Bandwidth Audio – the next big audio market][29]

interesting impasse, which is how to extract more money from consumers.  The bulk of users appear
happy with the audio quality they’re getting from their current hardware, as well as being satisfied
with their audio streaming services.  Unlike the video streaming industry, which is spending
billions on generating new content to attract subscribers, audio streamers are largely relying on
their back catalogues.  Whilst manufacturers and streamers have tried differentiation through
enhanced quality, specifically by providing hi-res or lossless codecs, they’ve found the take-up
disappointing, mainly because few consumers can notice the difference.

This poses a quandary for the industry.  They’ve invested significant amounts of money developing
new, high quality codecs, which can sample audio at rates which only bats are likely to hear.  The
components industry has also poured cash into developing new audio transducers, producing
micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) speakers, capable of rendering audio at frequencies way
beyond the limits of human hearing.  This technology has led to a new generation of microphones with
frequency responses which are flat up to 100kHz – a major step forward from common studio
microphones, which typically have frequency responses that start falling off at 14kHz.  Once again,
however, what they capture is beyond human hearing.

## Как работает Мой пропуск

Многофункциональный сервис оптимизации бизнес-процессов: отказ от лишних пластиковых карт,
автоматизация сложных рутинных процессов, оптимизация рабочего времени, легкое управление, упрощение
охранных решений, сбор статистики и не только

наведите на карточку

### Пластиковая карта

Добавляйте транспортную, банковскую или любую другую пластиковую карту для прохода без
дополнительного оборудования

### Динамический QR-код

Генерируйте коды на экране телефона и просто подносите их к считывателю для открытия доступа на
предприятие/в помещение

### NFC стикеры

Используйте мобильный телефон для считывания биометрических NFC меток, наклеенных на любую
поверхность точки прохода

### Виртуальная кнопка

Нажмите на кнопку в приложении или WEB-странице, чтобы дистанционно открыть проход к любой точке
предприятия

### BLE-технология

Осуществляйте проход по территории не вынимая телефон из кармана, благодаря бесконтактной технологии
BLE

## Frequently asked questions

How do I connect PPTControl to my computer?

PPTControl currently connects through Bluetooth Low Energy, also called BLE.

Bluetooth must be enabled on both devices, and PPTControl Desktop must stay open on the computer
while you use the remote.

My phone cannot find or connect to my computer. What should I do?

Make sure [PPTControl Desktop][16] is installed and open on the computer, and that Bluetooth is
enabled on both devices.

Make sure the phone and computer are not paired through normal Bluetooth settings. If they are,
remove that pairing on both devices, restart both devices, and connect again only through
PPTControl.

On Mac, also make sure the required permissions are granted. On Windows, check whether the Bluetooth
adapter supports Bluetooth Low Energy peripheral/server mode.

Can I view speaker notes in PPTControl?

Yes, with Pro, speaker notes are available for supported PowerPoint and Keynote presentations.

Open the presentation on the computer, connect PPTControl, and tap the notes icon in the mobile app.
Make sure the presentation actually contains notes and that both PPTControl apps are updated.

Which presentation apps does PPTControl support?

PPTControl is focused on **Microsoft PowerPoint**, **Apple Keynote**, and **Google Slides**.

Basic slide controls work best with the supported desktop workflows. Advanced features depend on the
presentation app and platform.

### GW16168 Edge AI Accelerator for Gateworks Industrial SBCs

The **GW16168** is an M.2 AI accelerator card designed to add powerful edge AI processing to
Gateworks industrial SBCs. Powered by the **NXP ARA240 Neural Processing Unit**, it delivers up to
**40 eTOPS** of AI performance for real-time workloads such as machine vision, robotics, and
predictive maintenance. With **16GB LPDDR4 memory** and a standard **M.2 PCIe interface**, it
enables efficient deployment of AI models directly on embedded and industrial IoT devices.

[Buy the GW16168 now][14]

### Wi-Fi HaLow M.2 Radio

on Gateworks industrial SBCs. Operating in the 850–950 MHz band, it supports data rates up to 43.3
Mbps and transmit power up to +26 dBm, enabling extended coverage and strong signal penetration
through walls and industrial environments. Powered by the Morse Micro MM8108 chipset, it provides
stable, low-power wireless communication for demanding IoT and embedded applications.

Wiliot connects physical items to the cloud using battery-free IoT Pixels, simple network
infrastructure, and AI-driven services. This transforms raw data into actionable insights for
smarter, more efficient operations.

###### IoT Pixels

Low-cost, battery-free Bluetooth sensors attach to items and harvest energy from ambient radio
signals to transmit data — such as location, temperature, humidity, and light.
